clue.text: Gardener and saint in novel association

parts.note: Adam, the first man, was set to tend the Garden of Eden
the Venerable Bede, Anglo-Saxon monk and historian, is a saint

explanation.surface: A gardener and a saint have been brought together in some new kind of club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel association' reads as a new society, but 'novel' is the definition: the two names associated make the title of George Eliot's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1859 book about a carpenter is titled with his name, making it a novel.

clue.text: Policeman to hound Yates hero

parts.note: to dog someone is to hound them
Berry Pleydell is the hero of Dornford Yates's 'Berry and Co' stories

explanation.surface: An officer harasses the hero of a thriller writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

clue.text: Lead a quiet life say by accident

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be spoken and its sound taken

parts.note: to lead a quiet life is to miss adventure

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into a sheltered existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By accident' reads as how the quiet life came about; 'by' is a link, recalling the coroner's verdict 'death by misadventure'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap or piece of bad luck is an unplanned mischance.

clue.text: Lobs as the Cockney tells the viewers

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the h, so the phrase is heard as spoken that way

parts.note: lobs are high balls

explanation.surface: A London tennis player describes his shots to the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, famous for dropping H: 'high balls' becomes ''igh balls', sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyes are the organs with which we see, so they are the viewers.

clue.text: Jones the butterfly?

definitions.meaning: The ... Jones is a play by Eugene O'Neill
the purple ... is a British butterfly

explanation.definitionFit: The word completes O'Neill's play title with Jones and also names a large purple butterfly.

clue.text: Nicholas' Nye needs first aid

parts.note: Nicholas Nye is the donkey in Walter de la Mare's poem of that name
1st, written with the figure as I, abbreviates first

explanation.surface: Nicholas Nye wants first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I, so 1ST gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone is to give them aid.

clue.text: I tolerate the language

parts.note: to tolerate is to put up with; PUT written upwards in this down light gives TUP

explanation.surface: I can bear the tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tolerate' stands for 'put up': PUT going up the column reads TUP, followed by I. Tupi is a South American Indian language of Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupi is spoken by indigenous peoples of Brazil and gave many words to Portuguese, so it is a tongue.

clue.text: Like Houdini he may act for others

definitions.text: Like Houdini he may act for others

parts.words: Like Houdini he may act for others
parts.note: Houdini performed daring escapes; a film double performs dangerous scenes in place of actors

explanation.surface: An escapologist who stands in for other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A film double who performs dangerous feats replaces the star in risky scenes.

clue.text: "Girl tied up" report causes fear

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is spoken and the sound taken

parts.note: a girl is a Miss, and tied up is trussed: MISS TRUSSED

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a bound girl spreads alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect or doubt someone is to fear what they may do, so suspicion and fear overlap.

clue.text: Prisons not opened for years

indicators.note: a word not opened has lost its opening letter

parts.note: cages are places of confinement, so prisons in a loose sense

explanation.surface: Jails left shut for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Ages' is informal for a very long time, many years.

clue.text: Notes about entering the aircraft industry in the short term

indicators.note: the notes and 'about' go inside, entering the word for the industry

parts.note: aviation is the business of building and flying aircraft
two musical notes, B and B
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Memos concerning a new arrival in aerospace, looking only at the near future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the short term' looks like a time phrase meaning soon; here it is the definition, a short term being a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened form of a word or phrase is a short term standing for the longer one.

clue.text: Attorney General maintained order frequently

indicators.note: putting the letters in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: The chief law officer often kept the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly, over and over, means often.

clue.text: The first composer to make a Journey

indicators.note: the first letter of the word 'The' is the one taken

parts.note: Maurice Ravel, French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: The leading composer sets off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To go from place to place is to journey somewhere.

clue.text: Cheerfulness needed to stop Mimi's disorder

indicators.note: Mimi's disorder suggests her letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone must be upbeat to cure Mimi of her illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' turns STOP and MIMI into the answer; 'needed to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful outlook, expecting things to go well, is a cheerful state of mind.

clue.text: No myths disseminated by Isaac Watts for instance

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: as printed the letters include an O; the setter's fodder should have had an I, as in 'In myths'

explanation.surface: Isaac Watts spread no legends abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed fodder 'No myths' has an O where the answer has an I; the setter meant letters like 'In myths'. Isaac Watts wrote hymns such as 'O God, Our Help in Ages Past'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Watts was an English writer of church songs, an example of a composer of sacred verse.

clue.text: Beautiful like Andromeda?

definitions.meaning: Andromeda is a constellation and galaxy in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both delightful and belonging to the sky, where the Andromeda galaxy lies.

clue.text: Duplicity of selling papers for a living

definitions.text: Duplicity of selling papers for a living

parts.words: Duplicity of selling papers for a living
parts.note: reads as a newsvendor's trade, but means betraying one's country by selling secret state papers

explanation.surface: A news vendor's job is called two-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country, for instance by passing secret documents to an enemy, is the gravest disloyalty.

clue.text: Official offender

definitions.meaning: a ... handles stolen goods, a crime

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a court officer managing a bankrupt's estate and a fence dealing in stolen goods.

clue.text: Exaggerate bowling speed

definitions.meaning: to overstate the worth of something
in cricket the ... is how fast a team bowls its overs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; the over rate measures how many a side bowls per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means overstating value and also the cricket measure of overs bowled per hour.

clue.text: Moves tried out on board

indicators.note: on board, inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, a steamship, the vessel one goes on board

indicators.note: tried out suggests the letters are worked into another shape

explanation.surface: Moves are tested on a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges TRIED into TRIDE, which goes on board the SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: Long steps taken in walking are the movements a walker makes.

clue.text: The story of a fight

definitions.meaning: the summary of a book's plot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a plot summary of a book and a heated dispute.

clue.text: The effervescence of a restorative spritzer!

indicators.note: of here means the letters are taken from within the two words that follow

explanation.surface: The fizz of a reviving white wine and soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit and spirit, a bubbling sparkle of character.

clue.text: Hefty staff strike

definitions.meaning: a thick heavy stick or club
to beat with such a club

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a short thick club and the act of beating someone with one.

clue.text: Being audacious, break in using a crowbar

parts.note: to break in is to enter a building
prising is levering open, as with a crowbar

explanation.surface: A bold burglar forces a way in with a jemmy.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing bold initiative and willingness to take risks is being daring.

clue.text: Ordered quite a lot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means neatly arranged and also, informally, fairly large, as in a decent sum.

clue.text: A road not to be in

parts.note: a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: A street nobody should enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent, out of the house, is not at home.

clue.text: Modest flutter of likely lad losing pound

indicators.note: a flutter is a nervous agitation, so the letters are stirred up
the pound letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A nervous little bet placed by a promising young man who loses a quid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' is British for a small bet, misleading with the pound. 'Losing' drops L from LIKELYLAD, leaving IKELYLAD for 'flutter of' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour proper to a well-bred woman is demure and decorous.

clue.text: Second one to make his mark is quick finisher

parts.note: a printer puts marks on paper

explanation.surface: The runner-up who leaves an impression has a fast finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner over a short distance finishes the race at high speed.
